conviction_note: Near non-result: every company-level item (1pt tariff-refund EPS in Q3, easy Q3-25 comp, Alani Nu/Rockstar distribution) sits inside what management already guided on 2026-07-09, and the bearish North America read is in two late-September downgrades and a 5% estimate cut; what is left is a washed-out positioning setup (52-week low, -9.2% in 20 days, calls bid at -4.6 skew) that agrees with the option market, against a guide that macro proxies (record September gasoline, crude-driven commodity inflation) put at risk. The findings sum to +0.2 and the scaled number is +0.27 (p_up 53 on abs_move 4.5); they agree in sign and both are small, because the print turns on the FY guide and nothing sourced says which way it goes.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue ~$25.0B and core EPS $2.30-2.31; two agreeing sources: https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/09/24/pepsico-holds-130-lows-ahead-of-oct-8-earnings-call/ ($2.30 / $25.00B) and https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/pep-stock-gets-a-downgrade-from-jp-morgan-firm-flags-frito-lay-weakness/cZMmCWWRBgW ($2.30 / $24.99B); Hudson Labs carries $25,008M (https://hudson-labs.com/research/pepsico-q3-2026-earnings-pep-revenue-and-outlook). Company guide FY26: organic +2-4%, core cc EPS +4-6%, trending to the low end (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/09/pepsico-pep-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue; the stock trades on EPS quality and the guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 1.90% of float, 3.2 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/PEP/short-interest/, via the sweep); not crowded. Skew_25d -4.61 vol points: calls priced above puts, 'upside paid'; put/call OI 0.84. Spot 124.14 at the 52-week low (0.0% from low), -27.2% from the high, -9.18% over 20 days, -2.04% over 5. Sell side de-rated into the print: Deutsche Bank Buy->Hold $155->$138 and TD Cowen $145->$133 on 2026-09-28, JPMorgan OW->Neutral $170->$138 on 2026-09-29; consensus EPS -5.24% over 90 days.

findings.finding: PEP goes into the print washed out: at its 52-week low, -9.2% over 20 days, three sell-side cuts/downgrades on 2026-09-28/29 and consensus EPS down 5.2% in 90 days, while the option market pays for upside (skew -4.6) and staples peers that beat and reaffirmed into similarly low bars in the past two weeks were bought (McCormick +4.8% premarket 2026-10-01, Conagra +3.2% 2026-09-30; General Mills -0.6% on a beat with 130bp margin contraction).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From the baseline: the two prints that came off depressed levels with a reaffirmed guide and a beat (2025-10 and 2026-02 windows) moved +4.23% and +4.93%; the July 2026 print (revenue beat, EPS miss by a cent, guide affirmed) moved -3.26%. The sweep checked the session tags: each baseline 'amc' date is the evening before a 06:00 ET release, so the close-to-close window is the same as for a bmo print and the history can be used.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the skew already leans up, so this agrees with the options market and is sized small. What is not in a single number is how the reaction function changed: if the de-rating were fully absorbed, the straddle would not sit below the name's own median reaction (3.41% vs 4.51%) and peers' beat-and-reaffirm prints would not have rallied.
findings.independence: Peer reactions from different sources: https://finviz.com/news/397767/mccormick-shares-rise-after-third-quarter-earnings-and-revenue-beat-estimates (MKC, 2026-10-01), https://finviz.com/news/397093/conagra-brands-shares-rise-32-after-first-quarter-earnings-beat (CAG, 2026-09-30), https://ts2.tech/en/general-mills-earnings-beat-leaves-its-stock-lower-as-margins-contract-130-basis-points/ (GIS, 2026-09-23, the counterexample). Estimate cut: https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/09/24/pepsico-holds-130-lows-ahead-of-oct-8-earnings-call/

findings.finding: Management told the market on 2026-07-09 that Q3 would carry 'approximately 1 point of EPS benefit from tariff refund claims likely in the quarter', against an easy comparison (Q3 2025 organic +1.3%, core EPS $2.29, -2%), so a $2.30 bar that is roughly flat year on year is set below what the guided components imply.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: revenue beat with a 1c EPS miss and an affirmed guide moved -3.26%; the line that moved the stock was the guide and North America margin, not the headline EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: It lands inside what the company guided, so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect. The refund is below the core line in substance and a one-off, with no path to the guide except to cover commodity inflation, which is how management framed it. Sized near 0.
findings.independence: Same fact reported by https://www.cfodive.com/news/pepsico-cfo-says-tariff-refunds-will-help-offset-inflation/825005/ (2026-07-14); Q3 2025 comps from https://hudson-labs.com/research/pepsico-q3-2026-earnings-pep-revenue-and-outlook. Both rest on the company's own call, so this is one finding.

findings.finding: Celsius's Q2 2026 10-Q confirms PepsiCo became primary US/Canada distributor of Alani Nu and Rockstar on top of Celsius, with Alani Nu orders lifted by the transition in Q2, so Q3 is PBNA's first full quarter of distributed-brand revenue. That points to a revenue beat that carries little margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 also beat on revenue and the stock fell 3.26%; this name has not paid for revenue beats that do not reach EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: Probably mostly in the $25.0B consensus (+4.9% reported growth against a 2-4% organic guide), and distributed brands are low-margin pass-through. Net of the rest: PFNA (the larger profit pool) is the line under pressure, so a beverage revenue lift cannot carry the print by itself.
findings.independence: Celsius's own Q2 call: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/celsius-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-06/ (the core Celsius brand fell 11.7% on 'inventory rebalancing', a partial offset). Same counterparty, so it counts once.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after PepsiCo last spoke show a weak US snack/food quarter: Campbell's Q4 FY26 (reported 2026-09-03) salty snacks retail sales -7.8%, chips -9.4%, in a 'highly competitive chips category'; Conagra Grocery & Snacks organic -2.0% (2026-09-30); General Mills organic flat on lower volume (2026-09-23). JPMorgan's tracked channel data say the Frito-Lay recovery stalled after Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: North America food weakness was the line that sold the July 2026 print (-3.26%) despite a revenue beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the downgrades of 09-28/29 cite exactly this channel data and the stock fell about 5% after them. The proxy is also ambiguous. Campbell's chip losses can be share ceded to Frito-Lay's price cuts of up to 15%, and Hershey's salty retail takeaway was +6.5% through 2026-06-28. Sized small.

findings.finding: The macro inputs management blamed for weak US volume and margin got worse at the end of the quarter. Management attributed soft US convenience volume to gas prices, and AAA shows September 2026 set a record monthly average of $4.33/gal (+$1.21 YoY on 2026-10-07), while Q3's own average was a little below Q2's (Jul $3.93, Aug $4.06 vs Apr $4.10, May $4.48). Q4 needs a profit step-up from productivity against higher costs, so 'low end of 4-6%' is at risk of a trim or a cautious Q4 framing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this name trades on: an affirmed guide with a low-end lean sold -3.26% in July 2026; reaffirmations off depressed levels were bought +4.2/+4.9% in 2025-10 and 2026-02.
findings.why_not_priced: Gas prices are public, and a guide trim is partly in a stock already at its low after the downgrades. If it were fully priced, the skew would not lean to upside and consensus would sit below the low end, but the bar sits at the low end. This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed for Q4, so it is sized as a proxy.
findings.independence: Monthly series: https://usgasgauge.com/gas-prices/history/2026; management's gas-price attribution: https://www.webull.com/news/15200195773236224 (Q2 call); Q4 reliance on productivity: https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/pep-stock-gets-a-downgrade-from-jp-morgan-firm-flags-frito-lay-weakness/cZMmCWWRBgW. The other findings do not share these documents.

outside_window.finding: Supreme Court to hear Rise Brewing's trademark appeal over 'Mtn Dew Rise' in the October 2026 term; the product was discontinued in 2024, so the exposure is damages only and no decision lands in the window.
JPMorgan reports PepsiCo plans low-to-mid-single-digit price increases on select chips and sodas for late 2026 or early 2027; it takes effect after the window unless it is announced on the call.

searched_and_found_nothing: Quarter-to-date Circana/Nielsen salty-snack scanner numbers for PepsiCo: no public figure found (octagonai page states none published as of 2026-08-29)
PepsiCo 8-Ks since the Q2 print: only a 2026-09-17 item 5.02 (Joaquin Duato elected to the board effective 2026-12-01); no restructuring, M&A or guidance 8-K
Elliott follow-through or bottling refranchising dated inside the window: nothing new; the company ruled out full refranchising in Dec 2025
Cause of the further drop from ~$128.5 (2026-09-29) to $124.14: no company-specific news found beyond the downgrades
The Q2 transcript PDF on investors.pepsico.com did not parse; used the fool.com transcript instead

baseline_tension: What I found mostly agrees with the baseline: the stock is washed out, the call-side skew leans up, and the small positive lean agrees with both. The one negative (guide risk from macro inputs) cuts against the skew, which is why it is sized as a proxy.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs, refunds): the Q3 tariff-refund/easy-comp finding is inside the guide and below the line in substance, so it was relabelled one_off and cut from +0.3 to +0.1
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): Alani Nu/Rockstar distribution helps PBNA revenue but is low-margin and the PFNA profit pool is the weak line, so cut from +0.2 to +0.1
Lesson 7 (positioning): the washed-out positioning finding agrees with the -4.6 call-side skew, so part of it is priced; cut from +0.8 to +0.6

Lesson 5 (proxy vs broad series): the peer snack weakness is ambiguous against Hershey's +6.5% salty takeaway and already in the JPM channel data, so cut from -0.3 to -0.2; the gas/commodity guide-risk proxy against the skew cut from -0.6 to -0.4

Lesson 1 / guidance-change likelihood: abs_move raised from 4.3 to 4.5 because a trim to the low end of the guide is plausible; p_up moved from 54 to 53 because the lean is a positioning proxy and not a document
